looks like i passed 60k followers, so figured it’d be a nice time to do another intro

i’m jason. i work on developer experience at openai.

since joining, i’ve been working on things like:

- helping developers move to codex
- openai cli, agents, realtime
- building codex for oss 
- motion design
- marketting

and more

this job is also pretty personal for me.

a few years ago, i injured both my hands badly enough that i could barely type, cook, or tie my shoelaces. for a long time i wasn’t sure i’d really be able to work on on a computer the same way again.

chatgpt was what first gave me a path back. it let me turn voice into writing, ideas into work, and eventually get back into tech and make a living again.

codex feels like the next step in that story. it gives me back a way to use a computer, not just a faster way to code. and what i feel like i’m getting back with codex, i hope people who are less computer-native can one day get to experience too, as we make progress toward a codex for everyone.

items.content:
here's a startup idea for you 🫵🏽

use google maps to find businesses you can sell $300-$1000 websites to, built in less than 5 minutes.

what is it?

70% of small local businesses still don't have a website. roofers, plumbers, dentists, hvac guys, fence installers.

they're getting calls from google maps alone, and they know they're losing the customers who want to research before calling. 

they just don't know how to fix it, and every web agency they've talked to quotes them $3,000 and a six-week timeline.

your tool builds the same one-page site in 5 minutes for $0 in tooling costs. same clean layout, same contact form, same "this business is real and trustworthy" energy. 

you charge $300-$1000 and deliver before the call ends

how to do it with a fully free stack ↓

1️⃣open google maps. type "[service] in [city]": roofers in scottsdale, plumbers in austin, hvac in phoenix. scroll past the top of the map pack. 

you're looking for businesses with 30+ five-star reviews and no website linked. these are pre-qualified leads, the reviews prove they do good work, the missing website proves they have a hole they already feel

2️⃣ install instant data scraper (free chrome extension), click the icon, hit csv. you get a spreadsheet of 100+ businesses in 90 seconds. 

names, phone numbers, ratings, review counts, websites. the ones with no website column are your prospects

3️⃣cold call the top 20. don't write a script. open with their name, the gap, and a question. "hey is this john? i was looking at your google listing and noticed you don't have a website linked. is that something you've been meaning to fix or is it not a priority right now?" 

cold calls to qualified prospects book meetings at ~10%. cold emails sit at 1-2%. it's not even close

4⃣on the booked call, paste their google maps details into claude and ask for a website prompt: services, hours, location, brand tone. take that prompt to google AI studio (free), paste it in, get a live working website in under 5 minutes. 

click publish. copy the link. share-screen it on the call. they're watching their own business become real on the internet for the first time

5⃣close on the same call. "this is what i'd build for you. want me to put it together this week?" $300 if they want a one-pager. 

$1000 if they want extras (lead form, gallery, blog setup, custom domain). invoice within the hour. deliver same day. same-day delivery is what separates this from every agency they've ever dealt with

6⃣once you own one niche, expand the offer. add review automation ($200/mo recurring, texts every customer a review link after the job). add an AI receptionist for missed calls ($300/mo recurring, captures the 62% of calls that go unanswered). 

now you're not a website guy, you're the entire digital infrastructure for that business. one-time $500 becomes $500/month.

google ai studio is free. instant data scraper is free. claude code runs on a $20/mo subscription. the only thing this costs you is the time to make 20 calls a week.

local service businesses in the U.S  for example spend $50B/yr on marketing and most of it is wasted on yellow pages, ads, and lead-gen platforms that mark up the cost 5x. 

a one-page website pays for itself the first month it converts a single customer. they know this. they just need someone who'll show up tomorrow and ship it.

you can run this as one person from a laptop. no team, no studio, no agency overhead. you need google maps, a phone, and a willingness to dial 20 numbers in a sitting and that's it.

items.title: Over the years being on X, one of the most common questions I get is whether or not someone should raise from VCs if the
items.content:
Over the years being on X, one of the most common questions I get is whether or not someone should raise from VCs if they "want to start their own fund". Just got another one of these today, so...

I can unequivocally say that for the vast majority of people, that is a terrible idea.

Firstly, most investment processes are not venture scale - both yourself and VCs are going to be sorely disappointed that delivering a 1bn of PnL as alpha is impossible for a large number of investment processes.

For a podshop, 50-100mn of PnL is still meaningful as long as it is diversified from other PnL streams. So they are willing to take a bet on non venture scale investment processes. Further, there are podshops of varying sizes - for tier 2 podshops, even a 5-10mn PnL is meaningful.

Secondly, which is the more important point, VCs are not at all equipped to handle any advice on the investment process OR the infrastructure surrounding an investment process at all. 

Outside of a very, very small number of VCs, most of them will vastly underestimate the required infrastructure to run a 24/7 trading operation and will not have the vocabulary to offer any help on the alpha generation side.

On the other hand, at podshops, you have dedicated teams supporting you in all operational, infrastructural and investment needs. And STILL, the average time taken for quant build out in podshops, with full infrastructure AND operational support is 6 to 12 months.

You typically come in with a "business plan", have senior PMs as mentors, and report to a business head that oversees your build out, allocates resources to you and advises you on all dimensions of your business. 

It is not an understatement to say that podshops are designed to get a new PM to market as safely, efficiently and effectively as possible. Their entire business is predicated on doing this very, very well.

So, no - unless you have a very specific reasons to raise money from VCs, the best incubator for a hedge fund are the podshops.
